document_check.note: The document is Akalp K, Ferreira JP, Soares CM, Ribeiro MJ, Teixeira AM. 'The effects of different types of exercises on cognition in older persons with mild cognitive impairment: A systematic review and meta-analysis', Archives of Gerontology and Geriatrics 126 (2024) 105541. It is a systematic review with meta-analysis, and it reports the cited interval: overall exercise effect size 1.165, 95% CI 0.741 to 1.589.

cited_result: Pooled effect of exercise versus control on global cognition in older adults with MCI: effect size (standardised difference in means) 1.165, 95% CI 0.741 to 1.589, random effects, 20 comparisons (df 19), I2 88%. This is the interval the review describes as starting at 0.74.
tool_reason: The cited result is a pooled estimate from a systematic review and meta-analysis of controlled exercise trials, so ROBIS applies.

domains.rationale: The protocol is registered, but the document gives no registration date, and the search is reported as finished in May 2024, after first submission in February 2024. The amnestic MCI population was dropped from the quantitative analysis after the fact. The criteria admit non-randomised controlled designs, exclude studies on a summed quality score, contain ambiguous clauses, and restrict to English-language reports from 2012 onward without giving a reason.

signalling.question: 1.1 Did the review adhere to pre-defined objectives and eligibility criteria?
signalling.quote: "The protocol for this SRMA was registered in the International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (INPLASY) under the protocol number INPLASY202450067." [p3]; "The last data collection from the databases was performed in May 2024." [p3]; "Received 28 February 2024; Received in revised form 25 May 2024" [p1]; "The amnestic MCI population was not included in our quantitative analysis due to insufficient data." [p5]

signalling.question: 1.2 Were the eligibility criteria appropriate for the review question?
signalling.quote: "(d) study design with control group" [p3]; "(f) that had poor quality assessment score according to Downs and Black modified checklist" [p3]

signalling.question: 1.3 Were eligibility criteria unambiguous?
signalling.quote: "(c) cognition measured with quantitative cognitive assessment (e.g. using cognitive tests such as MoCA, MMSE, TMT, etc.), and blood markers related with neuroinflammation and neuroprotection"; "(g) only MCI and amnestic MCI populations with exercise and control groups from the studies with different interventions"

signalling.question: 1.4 Were all restrictions in eligibility criteria based on study characteristics appropriate?
signalling.quote: "reports published from 2012"; "(f) that had poor quality assessment score according to Downs and Black modified checklist"

signalling.question: 1.5 Were any restrictions in eligibility criteria based on sources of information appropriate?
signalling.quote: "(f) reports published in English language"

domains.domain: Domain 2: identification and selection of studies
domains.rationale: Five bibliographic databases were searched, but with an RCT filter in PubMed and English-language and date filters that removed 2,704 records. The search string requires blood-marker or cognition terms AND mental-health terms. No supplementary search methods are reported, and one author did the title and abstract screening alone.

signalling.question: 2.1 Did the search include an appropriate range of databases/electronic sources for published and unpublished reports?
signalling.quote: "Web of Science, SPORTDiscus, Scopus and PsycInfo bibliographic databases" [p2]; "Relevant studies were identified using PubMED, SPORTDiscuss, Web of Science, Scopus, and PsycInfo databases." [p1]

signalling.question: 2.2 Were methods additional to database searching used to identify relevant reports?
signalling.quote: Searched for reference-list checking, citation searching, trial registries, grey literature or contact with experts to identify studies; none reported (authors were contacted only for missing data).

signalling.question: 2.3 Were the terms and structure of the search strategy likely to retrieve as many eligible studies as possible?
signalling.quote: "AND ("BDNF" OR "IGF-1" OR "IL-6" OR "TNF-α" OR "VEGF" OR ”irisin” OR “Cognition” OR "blood brain barrier"" ... "AND ("Mental health" OR "Cognitive assessment" OR “Memory” OR “neurogenesis” OR “neuroplasticity”"

signalling.question: 2.4 Were restrictions based on date, publication format, or language appropriate?
signalling.quote: "(b) published from 2012 and articles in English language for web of science database" [p2]; "2704 studies removed by filters" [p3]

signalling.question: 2.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in selection of studies?
signalling.quote: "Elimination according to the title and abstract was performed by one author (K.A.)."

domains.domain: Domain 3: data collection and study appraisal
domains.rationale: Nothing says data extraction was done in duplicate. Study appraisal used a summed Downs and Black quality score, done by one author, instead of a risk-of-bias tool for trials. Multiple cognitive outcomes were collapsed into one effect size per study with no stated selection rule, and 15 eligible studies contributed no data.

signalling.question: 3.1 Were efforts made to minimise error in data collection?
signalling.quote: "Selected studies and their characteristic were recorded as author’s name, sample size, exercise characteristics, cognitive outcomes and blood markers." (searched for independent or duplicate extraction; none reported)

signalling.question: 3.2 Were sufficient study characteristics available for both review authors and readers to be able to interpret the results?
signalling.quote: "Summary of study characteristics. Intervention and exercise characteristic that were used including study name, cognitive status of participants, type of exercise performed, intensity of exercise, sample size, cognitive outcomes, blood markers and duration of exercises."

signalling.question: 3.3 Were all relevant study results collected for use in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: "multiple outcomes of studies were computed and combined according to the literature and were presented as one effect size" [p3]; "we excluded 15 studies, from which we did not receive the necessary data for our systematic meta-analysis review, despite requesting more information by mail from the authors." [p3]

signalling.question: 3.4 Was risk of bias (or methodological quality) formally assessed using appropriate criteria?
signalling.quote: "The methodological quality assessment of the studies was performed using the modified Downs and Black checklist for randomized and non-randomized designs of health care interventions (Downs & Black, 1998)."

signalling.question: 3.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in risk of bias assessment?
signalling.quote: "Quality assessment of studies was performed by one author (K. A.)."

domains.rationale: Eligible studies and the amnestic MCI population were left out of the synthesis. Composite scores combine all cognitive domains. Two multi-arm studies enter twice, and the document does not say how their shared control groups were handled. Heterogeneity is very high (I2 88%, prediction interval -0.747 to 3.077) and was not explored. There is no sensitivity analysis. An asymmetric funnel plot was set aside on the basis of Egger's test alone, and study quality was not carried into the synthesis.

signalling.question: 4.1 Did the synthesis include all studies that it should?
signalling.quote: "In addition, we excluded 15 studies, from which we did not receive the necessary data for our systematic meta-analysis review" [p3]; "The amnestic MCI population was not included in our quantitative analysis due to insufficient data." [p5]

signalling.question: 4.2 Were all pre-defined analyses reported or departures explained?
signalling.quote: "we did not perform subpopulation analysis between amnesic MCI and non-amnesic MCI due to lack of comparable data." (protocol content not given in the document)

signalling.question: 4.3 Was the synthesis appropriate given the nature and similarity in the research questions, study designs and outcomes across included studies?
signalling.quote: "Varela et al 2012a and Varela et al 2012b - indicates same study with two different intensity exercise interventions, Yoon 2017a and Yoon 2017b - indicates same study with two different exercise interventions, Combined - indicates combination of multiple outcomes in one effect size" [p9]; "we performed the meta-analysis of cognition with composite cognitive scores which combined scores from all cognitive domains" [p15]

signalling.question: 4.4 Was between-study variation (heterogeneity) minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: "The value of the I-squared (I2) is equal to 88.045 indicating that the 88 % of variance observed, reflect the variance of true effects."; "we can estimate that the prediction interval is -0.747 to 3.077"

signalling.question: 4.5 Were the findings robust, e.g. as demonstrated through funnel plot or sensitivity analyses?
signalling.quote: "The funnel plot for the distribution of the observed studies was asymmetric (Fig. 2b)." ... "Therefore, there is no statistically evidence of publication bias." (no sensitivity analysis reported)

signalling.question: 4.6 Were biases in primary studies minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: "The studies included had good methodological quality (20–25) scores according to Downs and Black modified checklist"

domains.domain: Phase 3: risk of bias in the review
domains.rationale: The conclusions rank exercise types and recommend aerobic or resistance exercise, although the subgroup intervals overlap and heterogeneity is large. The only caveat is a general call for caution. MCI studies with no subtype stated are relabelled as non-amnestic. Interpretation leans on hypothesis-test language.

signalling.question: A. Did the interpretation of findings address all of the concerns identified in Domains 1 to 4?
signalling.quote: "Thus, aerobic or resistance exercise could be preferred and included in other exercise programs to prevent cognitive decline for persons with MCI."; "Due to limitations of study, the results should be interpreted with caution."

signalling.question: B. Was the relevance of identified studies to the review's research question appropriately considered?
signalling.quote: "Four studies included 259 participants with amnestic MCI whilst 18 studies included non-amnestic MCI population (Table 2)." (Table 2 labels these studies only as "MCI")

signalling.question: C. Did the reviewers avoid emphasising results on the basis of their statistical significance?
signalling.quote: "Therefore, the null hypothesis was rejected and we accepted the alternative hypothesis that exercise has an effect on cognition in older persons with MCI."

applicability.rationale: The pooled estimate covers MCI studies classed as non-amnestic, including studies that do not state a subtype, with amnestic MCI excluded. It pools programmes lasting from 6 weeks to 101 weeks (Table 2, p6-8) with no analysis by duration.

overall_rationale: All four ROBIS domains raise high concern. Screening and quality appraisal were each done by one reviewer, with language, date and RCT filters and no supplementary searching. Fifteen eligible studies and the amnestic population were excluded from pooling. Heterogeneous outcomes and multi-arm comparisons were pooled as composites. I2 of 88% was not explored, there were no sensitivity analyses, and the conclusions do not address these problems.
